newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-UEFA TO INVESTIGATE LIVERPOOL PLAYERS' T-SHIRT SLOGAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA TO INVESTIGATE LIVERPOOL PLAYERS' T-SHIRT SLOGAN.

text.p: A show of solidarity with 500 sacked dock workers by two Liverpool players during a European Cup Winners' Cup match will be investigated, UEFA said on Friday.

Robbie Fowler, who scored twice in Liverpool's 3-0 victory over Brann Bergen of Norway on Thursday, lifted his red Liverpool shirt after scoring his second goal to display the T-shirt underneath which read: "Support The 500 Sacked Dockers".
Steve McManaman admitted giving Fowler the T-shirt and wearing one himself in support of Liverpool dock workers at the centre of a two-year dispute.
"Such displays are against the rules and it will be discussed at the meeting but first we will have to get reports from the game officials," said UEFA spokesman Frits Alstrom.
UEFA regulations prohibit players from displaying political logos at matches.
The incident will be one of several discussed by UEFA's control and disciplinary committee when it meets on Tuesday.
The committee will also look into events that left eight Manchester United fans injured after a run-in with anti-riot police following Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final against Porto.
